title: Make MovieCard reusable
prompt:
Every card says "Arrival". Give `MovieCard` three props, `title`, `year` and `watched`, and use them: - `

` shows the title, a `

` shows the year. - Another `

` shows **Watched** when `watched` is true and **To watch** otherwise. Default `watched` to `false`. Then render these three cards in `App`, in this order: | title | year | watched | |---|---|---| | Arrival | 2016 | true | | Past Lives | 2023 | *(don't pass it)* | | Paddington 2 | 2017 | false |
hints: Destructure the props in the parameter list: `function MovieCard({ title, year, watched = false })`.
Numbers and booleans go in braces: `year={2016}`. A bare `watched` means `watched={true}`.
Choose the status text with a ternary: `{watched ? 'Watched' : 'To watch'}`.
explanation: `MovieCard` is now a function of its props. The default `watched = false` covers the Past Lives card, which doesn't pass the prop at all, so `watched` arrives as `undefined` and the default kicks in. Numbers and booleans need braces; a quoted `year="2016"` would pass a string, which looks the same here but behaves differently in arithmetic and comparisons.

checks.titles: Three cards titled Arrival, Past Lives and Paddington 2, in that order
checks.years: Each card shows its own year
checks.default-status: Past Lives and Paddington 2 show "To watch"
